title: The direct image of an injective module is acyclic for sections over every open
statement: Let $h:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; let $h_*\mathcal I$ be its direct image, the $\mathcal O_S$-module $V\mapsto\mathcal I(h^{-1}V)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then for every open $V\subseteq S$ and every $p>0$ one has $H^p(V,(h_*\mathcal I)|_V)=0$, where $(h_*\mathcal I)|_V$ is the restricted $\mathcal O_V$-module $W\mapsto(h_*\mathcal I)(W)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] and $H^p(V,-)$ is cohomology of $\mathcal O_V$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology]. In other words, $h_*\mathcal I$ is acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for the left exact functor $\Gamma(V,-)$ from $\mathcal O_S$-modules to $\mathcal O_S(V)$-modules, for every open $V\subseteq S$ (in particular for $V=S$). ($h_*\mathcal I$ need not be an injective $\mathcal O_S$-module, since $h^*$ need not be exact.)

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 01EX (lemma-pushforward-injective, line 1779), part (2); its proof uses Cech cohomology of f_*I via the covering f^{-1}(V_j) and Lemma 01EV (lemma-cech-vanish)

proof.text: **Step 1 (the Cech complex of $h_*\mathcal I$ is that of $\mathcal I$).** Let $V\subseteq S$ be open and $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of opens with $V=\bigcup_jV_j$; let $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$ be the corresponding covering of $S_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site]. Since $h$ is continuous, $h^{-1}V$ and the $h^{-1}V_j$ are open in $X$ and $h^{-1}V=\bigcup_jh^{-1}V_j$, so $\mathcal U=\{h^{-1}V_j\to h^{-1}V\}_{j\in J}$ is a covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$. In both Zariski sites the fibre products are the intersections with their inclusions (the categories are preordered sets), and $h^{-1}(V_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap V_{j_p})=h^{-1}V_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap h^{-1}V_{j_p}$. By the definition of the direct image [def-pc-module-pullback], $(h_*\mathcal I)(W)=\mathcal I(h^{-1}W)$ for $W\subseteq S$ open, and the restriction of $h_*\mathcal I$ along $W'\subseteq W$ is the restriction of $\mathcal I$ along $h^{-1}W'\subseteq h^{-1}W$. Hence, by the definition of the Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal V,h_*\mathcal I)=\prod_{(j_0,\ldots,j_p)}(h_*\mathcal I)(V_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap V_{j_p})=\prod_{(j_0,\ldots,j_p)}\mathcal I(h^{-1}V_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap h^{-1}V_{j_p})=\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ for every $p\ge0$, and the differentials, alternating sums of the restrictions along the inclusions omitting one index, agree term by term. So $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal V,h_*\mathcal I)=\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal V,h_*\mathcal I)=\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ for all $p$.

source.place: Lemma 01EX, proof, first paragraph (the displayed equalities of Cech complexes)

proof.text: **Step 2 (Cech vanishing for $h_*\mathcal I$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic] to the scheme $X$, the injective $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal I$, the open $h^{-1}V\subseteq X$ and its covering $\mathcal U=\{h^{-1}V_j\to h^{-1}V\}_{j\in J}$ of Step 1: $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $p>0$. By Step 1, $\check H^p(\mathcal V,h_*\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$, every open $V\subseteq S$ and every open covering $\mathcal V$ of $V$ (this is part (1) of Stacks 01EX).

source.place: Lemma 01EX, proof: 'Thus the first statement of the lemma follows from Lemma 01EP'

proof.text: **Step 3 (cohomology vanishes).** $h_*\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-pc-module-pullback], and by Step 2 it satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cech-vanishing-criterion] on the scheme $S$. That lemma gives $H^p(V,(h_*\mathcal I)|_V)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every open $V\subseteq S$ [pqf-def-cohomology], which is the first assertion.

source.place: Lemma 01EX, proof: 'The second statement follows from the first and Lemma 01EV'

proof.text: **Step 4 (the reformulation as $\Gamma(V,-)$-acyclicity).** Fix an open $V\subseteq S$. The functor $\Gamma(V,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_S)\to\Mod_{\mathcal O_S(V)}$ is additive and left exact, kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_S)$ being computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; $\Mod(\mathcal O_S)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], so its right derived functors $R^p\Gamma(V,-)$ are computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Choose an injective resolution $h_*\mathcal I\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. By the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives] (applied to $S$ and $V$), $(h_*\mathcal I)|_V\to\mathcal J^\bullet|_V$ is an injective resolution in $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$, so $H^p(V,(h_*\mathcal I)|_V)=H^p(\Gamma(V,\mathcal J^\bullet|_V))$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. Since $\Gamma(V,\mathcal G|_V)=\mathcal G(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal G)$ for every $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal G$, compatibly with morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], the complexes $\Gamma(V,\mathcal J^\bullet|_V)$ and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal J^\bullet)$ are equal, hence $R^p\Gamma(V,-)(h_*\mathcal I)=H^p(\Gamma(V,\mathcal J^\bullet))=H^p(V,(h_*\mathcal I)|_V)$, which is $0$ for $p>0$ by Step 3. So $h_*\mathcal I$ is $\Gamma(V,-)$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic]. For $V=S$, $(h_*\mathcal I)|_S=h_*\mathcal I$. (Stacks Lemma 01E1 (2).)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks Cohomology 01EX (2): kept; made self-contained (injective object, direct image h_* with its sections, the restriction (h_*I)|_V each cite their node; stmt_deps updated). The citer lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge uses only V = S, but the proof gives every V at once (the Cech criterion needs all opens). Proof in four steps following the proof of 01EX: (1) Cech complex of h_*I for an open covering of V equals that of I for the pulled-back covering of h^{-1}V (elementary, from the definitions of h_* and of the Cech complex on the Zariski site, fibre products = intersections); (2) 01EP for injective O_X-modules (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic); (3) the criterion 01EV for O_X-modules (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-module-cech-vanishing-criterion), stated with H^p(U,F|_U) as in pqf-def-cohomology; (4) the 'in other words' clause: R^p Gamma(V,-) on Mod(O_S) equals H^p(V,-|_V) by restricting an injective resolution (01E1 (2), via the statement of lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives and enough injectives). Existing Cech nodes are for abelian sheaves on a site (03AW, 03F9) or the small etale site; an injective O_X-module is not in general an injective abelian sheaf and module cohomology is not abelian cohomology without a comparison, so the module versions 01EP/01EV are new nodes (the site Cech complex def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex on X_Zar is reused). Mathlib: no Cech vanishing, no Cech criterion, no cohomology of O_X-modules (three kinds of search recorded on each node).
